newsitem.title: USA: NYS Medicaid may have been overcharged - comptroller.
newsitem.headline: NYS Medicaid may have been overcharged - comptroller.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller on Tuesday said that Medicaid might have overpaid millions of dollars for transporting patients by ambulances and taxi cabs, and recommended that the state improve its oversight.
"My auditors estimate that Medicaid paid more than $16 million for services that may or may not have been provided," McCall said in a prepared statement.
Noting that similar problems were found in 1989, McCall faulted the state Department of Social Services for failing to carry out the recommendations that were made then.
A larger pool of claims of almost $77 million for transportation that was paid to providers could not be matched to the actual medical services, he added.
New York State paid almost $529 million in Medicaid on 16.4 million of transportation claims for the 33 months ending in September, 1995.
New York City led the list with "potentially inappropriate" claims, accounting for 56 percent.
In another report, the comptroller saluted the state Child Support Enforcement Program for helping local districts do more to collect from absentee parents.

"They are on the right track and we hope they continue," he said, adding that in May 1995, state auditors found the program, which cost almost $182 million in the 1995-96 fiscal year, was not complying with federal rules. Washington funded two-thirds of the program.
